subject: Intro: Helix Analytics referral + escrow proposal
messages:
From: Helix Analytics <partners@helixanalytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@helixanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: partnership idea — referral + reseller lanes

Hi Logan / Ben,

Great to meet you both at the Integrators Summit last week — thanks again for taking the time. Helix is interested in two potential go-to-market lanes with Redwood: a referral path tied to lead-introductions (finder's fee + first-year revenue share) and a technical reseller option where Helix will resell a managed bundle to our enterprise customers.

Before we get into legal redlines we want to align on a handful of practical controls so both sides can forecast payouts:
- Lead registration process (proof of intro, MQL -> SQL handoff definitions)
- Initial rev-share percentages by ARR band and first/renewal year split
- Escrow or holdback structure for credits/chargebacks on churn
- Co-marketing and co-sell attribution window

I've attached a short intro deck that outlines Helix's pipeline and typical deal sizes. Can Redwood share a sample template for lead registration and a basic term-sheet we can use as a starting point? Ideally we'd get to a mutual action plan this month.

Thanks,
Rachel Diaz
Head of Partnerships | Helix Analytics
partners@helixanalytics.com
(555) 412-9841

Attachment: Helix_IntroDeck.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intro: partnership idea — referral + reseller lanes

Ben / Marissa — looped in per Helix's ask. Their intro deck looks promising; they have a few mid-market accounts with 100k–500k ARR potential and a steady pipeline.

Quick asks from my side before we send a formal term-sheet back:
1) Do we want to propose a dual-track (referral vs reseller) with different revenue splits? My thinking: referral = 12% first-year rev, 3% renewal; reseller = 18% reseller margin (gross-to-net to be defined).
2) Escrow: Helix asked for an escrow/holdback for chargebacks on churn. Ops prefers time-based holdback (quarterly releases) compared to event-based escrow.
3) Lead proof: we should require a single documented POC email thread + earliest HubSpot lead create timestamp. Use the attached lead-registration-template.

Marissa — can you draft a concise term-sheet (1 page) that covers the above and includes a simple waterfall example (first-year payout calculation + clawback window)? Ben — flag any ops constraints on the reseller margins/settlement timing.

I'll reply to Rachel with the draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---- Forwarded message attached: Helix_IntroDeck.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rachel Diaz <partners@helixanalytics.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: partnership idea — referral + reseller lanes

Hi Rachel — nice to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the deck. I attached a concise draft term-sheet and a lead-registration template for Helix to review. High-level notes inside the term-sheet:

- Referral lane (finder): 12% payout on first-year recognized revenue when Redwood invoices the customer and the lead registration is accepted. 3% on renewals for first two renewal cycles. Clawback window = 12 months from invoice in the event of customer cancellation; clawback amount netted from subsequent payouts.
- Reseller lane: 18% margin to Helix on Redwood list price when Helix resells and provides support. Gross-to-net adjustments (discounting, credits) reconciled monthly; payment terms 60 days after Redwood recognizes revenue.
- Escrow / Holdback: propose a quarterly holdback pool equal to 8% of gross payout for first 12 months; releases quarterly after a 90-day observation period. This avoids a third-party escrow account but provides a predictable reserve for chargebacks.
- Lead registration proof: earliest inbound email or HubSpot lead create timestamp plus an intro email thread with the customer's buying manager. Template attached.
- Co-marketing: co-op credits capped at $15k per calendar year; marketing leads follow referral lane rules unless a co-sell motion is explicitly tracked in HubSpot.

Attachments: proposed-revshare-term-sheet.xlsx (attachment stub), lead-registration-template.docx (attachment stub)

Rachel — two quick operational asks before we finalize: 1) Can you confirm Helix's typical payment terms to partners (Net30/Net60)? 2) Any customers in the next 60 days we should fast-track for early onboarding?

If the above looks good we can convert the term-sheet into a redline-ready clause set for legal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com

Note: included the waterfall example on page 2 of the spreadsheet (example deal: $200k ARR, first-year recognized revenue $150k -> referral payout $18k before holdback).

From: Rachel Diaz <partners@helixanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Intro: partnership idea — referral + reseller lanes

Marissa / Logan / Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear proposal. Helix is aligned on the dual-track approach. Quick answers:
- Payment terms to partners: typically Net45; we can accept Net60 for the reseller lane if required.
- Pipeline: two named accounts (MavenGrid, BorderTech) that could convert within 45–90 days. I'll push to get the intro threads and confirm lead-create timestamps by Monday morning.
- Escrow: the quarterly holdback model is acceptable to our finance team — appreciate the operational simplicity.

Next steps from Helix: I'll upload the signed partner intake form, push the two named account intros into HubSpot, and confirm the POC email threads. Once you confirm the final redline window we'll send counters.

Appreciate it — excited to get the first pilots running.

Best,
Rachel Diaz
